class.name: VegetationField3D
class.brief_description: Places the plants of a [Biome] over a [TerrainDataMap3D].
class.description: Places plants the way Horizon Zero Dawn does (van Muijden, GDC 2017): the map is cut into tiles of [member tile_size]; for each [PlantSpecies] in the [Biome]'s order, a tiled Poisson-disk pattern (Bridson 2007) is laid over each tile and each point is kept when its random rank is below the species' density times its rules there, so density changes smoothly and stays evenly spread. Plants stand on the map's height, keep later species out of their footprint, and are drawn as one [MultiMeshInstance3D] per mesh per tile (internal children, not saved). The result depends only on the map, the biome and [member seed].

method.name: get_bark_detail_node
method.description: The [BarkDetail3D] the field made (see [member bark_detail]), or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_contact_trample_at
method.description: The bend (world xz, length 0..1) of the ground cover's trample field at [param position], where this field keeps it: with no [GrassField3D] in the scene, one VegetationField3D keeps the field every plant reads (grass_trample_map), pressed by the bodies in the grass_trample and world_contact groups, so herbs, ferns and heath lay down under bodies on bare ground too. Zero where a [GrassField3D] keeps it.

method.name: get_far_match_stats
method.description: The live-view match of the far colour ([member far_match_view]): [code]shade[/code] (the factor on the far colour where it stands for plants, the global [code]vegetation_far_shade[/code]), [code]ratio[/code] (covered over bare ground near, against the same far, at the last look), [code]groups[/code] (sample groups used), [code]round[/code], [code]state[/code] (0 idle, 1 waiting, 2 reading), [code]misses[/code] (looks in a row that found too few spots) and [code]gain[/code] (how strongly the on-screen contrast follows the shade). For checking a scene's far blend, since global shader parameters cannot be read back at runtime.

method.name: get_far_shade
method.description: The current factor on the far colour where it stands for plants (see [member far_match_view]); 1.0 when the match is off or has not run.

method.name: get_far_shell_column_count
method.description: How many columns the [member far_shell] holds now.

method.name: get_near_radius
method.description: The global shader parameter [code]vegetation_near_radius[/code]: the smallest [member stream_radius] of the fields streaming now, so a terrain far blend has taken over before the first plants run out; 0 when none streams.

method.name: get_spring_wetness_at
method.description: The wetness round a desert spring at [param global_position] (x and z), as [constant PlantSpecies.RULE_SPRING] reads it: 0 dry to 1 at the water, -1 off the sand seas. Read with the last placement, and only when a species uses the rule.

method.name: add_canopy_loss
method.description: A felled tree or snapped crown: every placed crown centred within [param radius] of [param xz] keeps only [param keep] of its leaf area. [method get_shade_at] sees it at once, and every later repaint of the canopy ([member WeatherMap3D.canopy_map] through [member weather_map]) takes it out again, so streaming does not restore a felled crown. The caller cuts the live canopy map itself ([TreeWind3D] does).

method.name: clear_canopy_losses
method.description: Forgets every [method add_canopy_loss]: the next repaint restores those crowns.

method.name: get_canopy_losses
method.description: The felled crowns from [method add_canopy_loss]: x, z, radius and the leaf area kept, each.

method.name: get_springs
method.description: The desert springs the last placement used, from the terrain ([method TerrainGenerator3D.get_springs]): x, the water's level, z and the discharge in litres a second (w; 0 takes the pools' default) each. For the water and terrain systems to put a pool there. Empty unless a species uses [constant PlantSpecies.RULE_SPRING].

method.name: get_stream_stats
method.description: Main-thread cost of [member streaming]: [code]tiles[/code] (placed tiles held), [code]jobs[/code] (tiles being placed on workers), [code]frame_max_msec[/code] (the slowest frame since the last call, which resets it) and [code]publish_msec[/code] (handing the last maps to the renderer).

method.name: get_stream_tile_count
method.description: The number of placed tiles held around the centre while [member streaming].

method.name: get_trunks_near
method.description: Returns the placed trees within [param radius] metres of [param center] whose meshes carry TreeGenerator's [code]tree_colliders[/code], each once, as a [Dictionary]: [code]base[/code], [code]up[/code] (the trunk's axis), [code]height[/code], [code]radius_base[/code], [code]radius_top[/code], [code]segments[/code] (the trunk's capsules up to [param height] metres, each [code][a, b, radius][/code]), all in world space; [code]preset[/code] (the species' [code]preset[/code] meta), [code]species[/code], [code]variant[/code], [code]basis[/code], [code]custom[/code] (the instance's custom data) and [code]seed[/code] (from where it stands). For close-up bark detail.

method.name: is_still_frozen
method.description: With [member still_shot]: [code]true[/code] once it has settled and stopped updating.

method.name: is_stream_idle
method.description: [code]true[/code] once every tile within [member stream_radius] is placed and drawn and the maps are up to date. [signal populated] is emitted each time this becomes [code]true[/code].

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes every placed plant.

method.name: get_crowns_in
method.description: The placed crowns reaching into a world rectangle (x and z), seven floats each: x, z, crown radius, the crown's top and its base (lowest foliage) above the ground, 1 for a conifer or 0, and the crown's opacity. [PhysXFireSpread3D] reads them to light crowns.

method.name: get_deadwood_at
method.description: The placed log whose side is nearest the point, seen from above, if it is within [param reach] metres, past any thinner than [param min_radius]: [code]side[/code] (metres from its side, negative under it), [code]radius[/code], [code]top[/code] (the height of its upper surface over the point), [code]normal[/code] and [code]across[/code] (the level unit direction from its axis to the point). Empty when none is that close. Logs are the placed plants of species with the meta [code]deadwood[/code] whose meshes carry [code]tree_deadwood_axis[/code] (see [member PlantSpecies.deadwood_rule]).

method.name: get_deadwood_count
method.description: How many logs the last placement put down (with their axes).

method.name: add_plant_removal
method.description: Takes plants away for good: no plant of [param species] (its index in the [Biome]; -1 any) within [param radius] of [param position] (horizontal) is placed again. Streamed tiles there are placed again without them; a populated field populates again.

method.name: clear_plant_removals
method.description: Forgets every [method add_plant_removal]; the plants come back.

method.name: get_instances_near
method.description: The drawn instances of [param species] within [param radius] of [param position] (horizontal), one [Dictionary] each: [code]transform[/code] (global) and [code]mesh[/code].

method.name: get_plant_removals
method.description: The removals: x, z, radius and species (-1 any) each.

method.name: get_flood_replaced_tiles
method.description: Returns how many streamed tiles were placed again because the flood marks over them changed ([method WorldWater.high_water_at]: a flood peaked, fell or aged), for species that read them ([constant PlantSpecies.RULE_HIGH_WATER]).

method.name: get_placements
method.description: Returns the world positions of the plants of species [param species] (its index in the [Biome]) from the last [method populate].

method.name: get_plant_count
method.description: Number of plants placed by the last [method populate].

method.name: get_populate_time_msec
method.description: Time the last [method populate] took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_cover_texture
method.description: The last cover map built with [member cover_map_enabled], or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_conifer_at
method.description: Share of the canopy over [param global_position] that is needle-leaved ([member PlantSpecies.canopy_conifer]), weighted by how much each crown covers it: [code]0.0[/code] under broadleaf trees or in the open, [code]1.0[/code] under conifers.

method.name: get_floor_shader_code
method.description: Shader code for terrain materials: [code]forest_floor(world_pos, albedo)[/code] returns the ground's albedo with the forest floor laid over it where the canopy closes, leaf litter under broadleaf crowns, needles over duff with feather moss drifts under conifers, a patchwork in mixed stands. It reads the [code]forest_floor_map[/code] and [code]forest_floor_rect[/code] global shader parameters (see [member forest_floor_enabled]). Use it in a fragment shader. [method GrassField3D.get_ground_shader_code] includes it and its [code]grass_ground()[/code] calls it, so materials that use the grass ground get the litter too. It also gives [code]vegetation_far(world_pos, albedo, camera_pos)[/code]: call it after [code]grass_ground()[/code] with [code]CAMERA_POSITION_WORLD[/code]. Where plants with a [member PlantSpecies.far_color] grew, it blends their colour into the ground as the plant shader thins them away with distance, with the same curve: none up to 35% of the species' range, all of it at the range. It reads the [code]vegetation_far_map[/code], [code]vegetation_far_rect[/code] and [code]vegetation_far_range[/code] global shader parameters, published after each [method populate] that places such plants.

method.name: get_stream_pending
method.description: While [member streaming]: the tiles still being placed or waiting to be swapped in, plus one for each change (a burn scar placed, moved or aged, holes, the stand) not yet sent to its tiles. [code]0[/code] once the field shows the world as it is now. A still shot taken right after a change (a [WorldBurnScar3D] added after the plants were built) waits for [code]0[/code] first, as for the path tracer's pending surfaces. Always [code]0[/code] when not streaming.

method.name: load_floor_scans
method.description: Loads the scanned forest floor detail named in [code]floor_scans.cfg[/code] under [param dir] (the art repository's terrain layers): sections [code][leaves][/code], [code][needles][/code] and [code][moss][/code], each with a [code]scan[/code] folder name and a [code]tile[/code] in metres. Each scan's luminance over its mean is used as detail only, so the floor keeps its own colours. Under broadleaves it textures the humus between the leaf sprites, under conifers the needle duff, and it gives the moss drifts their structure. Sets the [code]forest_scan_leaves[/code], [code]forest_scan_needles[/code], [code]forest_scan_moss[/code] and [code]forest_scan_tile[/code] global shader parameters read by [method get_floor_shader_code]. Returns the number of scans loaded; a missing folder warns and leaves the floor without scanned detail.

method.name: make_game_trails
method.description: A network of game trails linking [param goals] (the places animals use: cover, feeding lawns, water) over the [TerrainDataMap3D] [param data_map] within [param area] (world xz). Every pair of goals within reach is routed by least cost, nearest pairs first; slope, water and a seeded roughness raise a cell's cost and traffic already routed over it lowers it, so routes merge into a branching network (the active walker model of trail formation). Returns worn paths in the form [member paths] and [member GrassField3D.paths] take: Dictionaries of [code]points[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]passes[/code] a year and [code]kind[/code] ([code]"game_trail"[/code]), one per stretch of equal traffic. [param options]: [code]cell[/code] (grid metres, 2), [code]reach[/code] (furthest goals linked, 250 m), [code]passes[/code] (a year along one link, 500), [code]width[/code] (tread, 0.35 m), [code]attraction[/code] (0..0.9, how much cheaper worn ground is, 0.6), [code]max_slope_deg[/code] (40), [code]ford_depth[/code] (deepest water waded, 0.4 m), [code]roughness[/code] (0.35), [code]seed[/code] (1).

method.name: get_crowns_near
method.description: The placed crowns reaching within [param radius] of [param position] (horizontal distance), one [Dictionary] each: [code]position[/code] (the stem's foot, world), [code]preset[/code] (the species' [code]preset[/code] meta, or -1), [code]height[/code], [code]crown_base[/code] and [code]crown_radius[/code] in metres, scaled by the instance. [code]conifer[/code] is true for a needle-leaved crown. Height and crown base come from the species' first mesh's [code]crown[/code] meta (height, crown base, crown radius, unscaled) when it has one, else the crown's top and a third of it.

method.name: get_rock_chunk_count
method.description: The chunks (32 m squares) of the [member rock_field]'s stones fetched so far.

method.name: get_shade_at
method.description: Canopy shade at [param global_position], from 0 (open sky) to 1 (dense crown), from the plants of species with [member PlantSpecies.canopy_radius] placed by the last [method populate]. Each crown stops [member PlantSpecies.canopy_opacity] of the light under its core, fading out a little past its rim; overlapping crowns multiply their transmission. Species with a [member PlantSpecies.shade_range] are placed by it, so list canopy species first in the [Biome].

method.name: get_light_at
method.description: The light plants grow in at [param global_position]: the open sky left by [method get_shade_at] times how sunny the slope is against the map's mean (the [TerrainDataMap3D] climate's shortwave; 1 without climate), from 0.3 to 1.5. Leaves and grass blades are tinted by it (darker and bluer in shade, paler in full sun), and the far cover map's grass colours take the same tint.

method.name: get_litter_at
method.description: Broad-leaf litter fallen at [param global_position], from 0 (none) to 1 (a full mat), from the crowns placed by the last [method populate]. Under a crown it is full; past the rim it thins over about 6 m, the drift of leaves blown out of a stand into its edge or a clearing (Ferrari and Sugita 1996), farther downwind ([member litter_wind]). Needle-leaved crowns add none. Species with a [member PlantSpecies.litter_range] are placed by it.

method.name: get_litter_drift_at
method.description: How the wind has gathered fallen leaves at [param global_position] ([constant PlantSpecies.RULE_LITTER_DRIFT]): 1 where they lie as they fell; up to 2.5 in hollows (the ground's depth under its ring at 2.5 and 6 m) and within about half a metre of trunks, logs and rocks, deepest on their downwind side ([member litter_wind]); down to 0.15 on crests and slopes over 25 to 45 degrees. The placement scales [method get_litter_at] by it (capped at 1) for species with a [member PlantSpecies.litter_range].

method.name: get_stand_shade_at
method.description: The shade the ground gets from the stand: [method get_shade_at] weighed by how closed the canopy is over about 5 m around, on half-metre cells after [method populate]. Under a lone open-grown tree it stays low, so the sward and no litter mat stay there; under a closed canopy it equals the shade. [GrassField3D] reads it for its shade rule, and the forest floor's litter follows it.

method.name: get_sward_litter_at
method.description: The field's undergrowth litter at a point ([member PlantSpecies.litter_color]): the species' litter colours weighed by how much each covers, in rgb, and the combined cover in alpha. Weighed as [method get_sward_shade_at] is. Main thread.

method.name: get_sward_shade_at
method.description: How much of the grass the field's tall undergrowth shades out at a point, 0 to 1: each species with [member PlantSpecies.sward_shade] weighed by where it grows (its density, rules, patches and shade rule, eased so a stand's sparse margin keeps its grass), not by the placed plants, so it does not change as the field streams. [GrassField3D] reads it through [member GrassField3D.undergrowth_field]. Main thread.

method.name: populate
method.description: Places every species over the whole data map, replacing earlier plants. Returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] without a [member biome] or a baked map.

method.name: queue_populate
method.description: Populates at the end of the frame, once.

method.name: sample_lateral_cover
method.description: Returns the placed plants' frontal area index at a global point: the area they show the wind ([member PlantSpecies.wind_frontal_area] times each plant's scale squared) per square metre of ground, spread over a 1 m grid, at most 0.5. Put this field in [code]GroundSurface3D.wind_shelters[/code] and its plants shelter blowing sand and trap it (Raupach's drag partition): dune grass builds hummocks round itself.

method.name: get_path_passes_at
method.description: Returns the walkers a year at [param position] from [member paths], 0 off every path.

method.name: get_species_range
method.description: The range the biome's species [param species] is drawn to: its [member PlantSpecies.visibility_range], or for a small species ([member PlantSpecies.detail_size] above 0, with [member detail_reach] on) the distance where that size is still [member detail_pixels] tall, when that is further, up to [member detail_max_range].

method.name: get_biome_share_at
method.description: The share of the ground at [param position] this field's [member biome_channel] holds in [member biome_map]: normalised when the painted channels sum past 1, and 1 outside the map.

method.name: notify_biome_map_changed
method.description: Places again the tiles in [param area] (metres; empty for all) after [member biome_map] was painted.

method.name: notify_density_mask_changed
method.description: Places again the tiles in [param area] (metres; empty for all) after [member density_mask] was painted.

members.member: A density mask over [member density_mask_rect], read once per [method populate] (bilinear). Each species with a [member PlantSpecies.mask_channel] multiplies its suitability by that channel (or by one minus it with [member PlantSpecies.mask_invert]), the way open-world tools paint or generate per-layer density maps (Unreal's landscape layer weights for grass types, Unity's terrain detail maps, Horizon Zero Dawn's density maps per ecotope). Paint a clearing as 0 in the trees' channel and the meadow's species can read the same channel inverted. Outside the rect the mask counts as 1.
The world rectangle (x and z, metres) that [member density_mask] covers.

Close-up bark on this field's trunks: when a species has trunks ([code]tree_colliders[/code] mesh meta), the field makes a [BarkDetail3D] as an internal child, linked to the field and following the camera. A [BarkDetail3D] the scene puts under the field itself is kept instead. Switch off for tests and benches that do not need it.
The species to place.

Another [VegetationField3D] whose crowns also shade this field's plants, as [member GrassField3D.canopy_field] does for grass. Its shade and conifer share combine with this field's own crowns (transmissions multiply), so a small herb field around the camera grows its shade plants under a large forest field's trees.

Drylands: no cover plants (herbs, grasses, shrubs; not trees, ground features or bare-ground species: [constant PlantGenerator.PRESET_SOIL_CRUST], [constant PlantGenerator.PRESET_DESERT_ANNUALS] and species with the meta [code]bare_ground[/code]) on the climate's bare soil patches, the pattern [member GrassField3D.climate_bare] and the terrain material use. Read as tiles are placed. No climate: no effect.
Texel size of the cover map ([member cover_map_enabled]), in metres.
A [GrassField3D] whose rules and far colour ([method GrassField3D.get_far_color]) are the cover map's bottom layer.

More [GrassField3D] layers under [member cover_grass] for the cover map, top down: an undercoat that fills the gaps between patches of tall grass. Each layer's share is its rules' suitability over what the layers above leave, in its own [method GrassField3D.get_far_color]; without them the gaps read as bare ground from afar.

Builds the plant cover seen from far above over the whole [member data_map] and publishes it as the [code]terrain_cover_map[/code] (RGBA8: sRGB cover colour, alpha the share of ground hidden) and [code]terrain_cover_rect[/code] globals, which [TerrainMaterial3D]'s far blend reads. It comes from the species' rules, not the placed plants, so it covers the map while only the camera's surroundings are placed ([member streaming]): crowns from above (the share each canopy species shades over its own placement pattern at its local density, spread by the crown radius), the plants with a [member PlantSpecies.far_color] under them by the shade and stand type those crowns give, and the [member cover_grass] under those. Built on worker threads on [method populate] or when streaming starts (about 70 ms for a square kilometre of oak wood at 4 m); on a streaming field, setting this, [member cover_grass] or [member cover_grass_layers] later builds it again at once, so there is no need to call [method populate] (which would place the whole map and stop the streaming).
The [TerrainDataMap3D] that gives height, slope, wetness and water. Its area is the area planted.
The furthest a small species is drawn by [member detail_reach], in metres.
How many pixels tall a small item still is where [member detail_reach] stops drawing it.

Small species ([member PlantSpecies.detail_size] above 0: fallen leaves, twigs, mosses, small rosettes, seedlings) are drawn as real geometry out to where they are still [member detail_pixels] tall at the camera's field of view and the viewport's height (the rule [RockField3D]'s ground detail uses), instead of their hand-set [member PlantSpecies.visibility_range], when that is further. Every species with a range is cut into cells of half its range so the range is measured near each plant, and the path tracer instances the small species' shapes (see [method RenderingServer.multimesh_set_rt_instanced]). Read when the field is placed or starts streaming.
A viewport height in pixels for [member detail_reach] in place of the viewport's own (0).

If [code]true[/code], the far colour that replaces plants past their [member PlantSpecies.visibility_range] is matched to the plants on screen: a few frames after the maps are built (and again when the camera has moved a fifth of the range), the field reads back the rendered image along arcs at covered and bare ground spots near the camera (where plants are drawn) and just past the range (where the far colour is), and scales the far colour where it stands for plants (the global [code]vegetation_far_shade[/code]) until the covered-to-bare ratio matches, within 3%. This carries the plants' own darkening of the ground (their shadowed depths and self-shadow) into the far colour, so the ground does not brighten into a lighter band where the plants end. While the viewport is path traced the match waits, keeping the raster frames' shade. See [method get_far_match_stats].

While [member streaming], how far species with a range go on as real plants, as a multiple of their range: from half the range they thin with the square of the distance, by rank so the field stays even, and the plants left grow up to 1.6 times to hold their cover, fading out over the last quarter. Each streamed tile holds only the plants its distance keeps and is rebuilt as the camera comes closer. Small items with a [member PlantSpecies.detail_size] keep their pixel reach. [code]1[/code]: no tail, the plants fade out by their range.

While [member streaming], the plant cover past the streamed plants out to [member far_shell_range], as one surface draped over the ground: each cell reads every species with a range and a [member PlantSpecies.far_color] from its own rules (suitability with its patches, times its density and the ground it hides), stands at their expected height by cover, lumped by a hash, in their mean far colour, and thins down into the ground where the cover thins. It rises out of the ground inside the streamed plants' thinning. Cells 2 m wide to 400 m, 8 m to 1600 m, 32 m past it. Species that need canopy shade, sand, a coast or pools are left out, and so are trees (a [member PlantSpecies.canopy_radius] or a far tail of their own): their own far forms carry them.

Where the [member far_shell]'s cells are fine enough, it opens into clumps and gaps (three octaves at 7, 19 and 53 m, each fading out as the cells grow past about a third of its size) with shade at the clumps' feet, so about each stand's cover share of the ground is under clumps, as heath, gorse and scrub grow. Off: an even mass by cover.
How far the [member far_shell] reaches, in metres.

If [code]true[/code], plants past their [member PlantSpecies.visibility_range] are drawn as real volume out to [member far_volume_range] instead of leaving only the ground's far colour: per tile and species, a voxel shell of the placed plants' leaf cover, porous where the stand is thin, lumpy rather than boxy, in the species' [member PlantSpecies.far_color], crossfading in as the plants thin out. Plain geometry, so path tracing sees the same shell. Plants lower than half a [member far_volume_cell] are left to the far colour. Takes effect at the next [method populate] or streamed tile.
The far volume's voxel size in metres. Smaller is finer and costs more triangles.
How far the far volume is drawn, in metres; past it only the ground's far colour remains.

Downwind lean of the leaf drift ([method get_litter_at]): its direction is the way the leaf-fall wind blows toward (x, z), its length (up to [code]0.8[/code]) how much farther the drift reaches downwind and the less upwind. Zero: taken from the [member weather_map]'s wind at placement, half a lean at 10 m/s.

Rocks on the ground that no plant grows through: each a disc (x, ground y, z, radius), the radius where the rock meets the soil, for example from [method TerrainGenerator3D.get_boulders]. A ground plant's stem keeps 3 cm off a rock, a tree's trunk foot and a log's length keep clear of it. A ground plant's leaves reach at most 8 cm in over a rock's foot: one that would reach farther grows smaller and leans away from the rock (down to 45% of its size), or is not placed. Give the widest radius of a rock that bulges out above the soil. Give the same list to the [GrassField3D] layers. Takes effect at the next [method populate].

A [RockField3D] whose stones the plants keep out of, as [member obstacles] does, fetched with [method RockField3D.get_obstacles] round each tile just before it is placed and kept in 32 m chunks: no world-wide list of every stone is made, and only the rock cells near the tiles are placed. The placements are the same as with that rock field's stones given as [member obstacles]. Both can be set: the plants keep out of both. Setting it fetches the stones again.

The widest stone footprint (radius at the soil, metres) the [member rock_field] is expected to have: each tile fetches the stones this far past the reach of its plants. A warning is printed if a wider stone is fetched.
The smallest stone (its size, metres) of the [member rock_field] the plants keep out of, the [code]min_size[/code] of [method RockField3D.get_obstacles].

For still shots on a tight memory budget: once [member streaming] has settled round its centre, the field stops streaming and drops its placement patterns until the centre moves 0.5 m. [method is_still_frozen] says when it has settled.

Optional, one per [member stone_tops] entry: the surface normal of each cap, measured on the stone (for example by a ray down onto its collision hull). With them, a cap is a flat patch of the stone's surface: a plant there is set on the plane through the cap's point and tilted to its normal, which fits sloping and flat stone faces; give a cap radius only as wide as the surface stays within about a centimetre of that plane. Ignored unless it has as many entries as [member stone_tops]. Takes effect at the next [method populate].

The caps of stones that [member PlantSpecies.stone_top] species grow on: each (x, top y, z, cap radius), the stone's highest point and the radius of its rounded top, for example from [code]RockField3D.get_stones()[/code] ([code]top[/code], and about half the [code]footprint[/code]). A plant there is set down the cap as a dome of that radius from the top and tilted with it (or on the cap's plane, with [member stone_top_normals]), 3 mm into the stone. Takes effect at the next [method populate].
If [code]true[/code], populate when ready (once the map is baked) and again whenever the map is baked again, after terrain edits.
Seed of the point patterns. The same seed gives the same plants.
Main-thread time per frame for adding placed tiles to the scene while [member streaming], nearest first. One tile always goes in, so a frame can run over by one tile's cost.
While [member streaming], the canopy map, the stand shade and the forest floor map cover this far around the centre (half-metre cells); the far colour map covers [member stream_radius].

An [OasisSprings3D] whose pools' outlines ([method OasisSprings3D.get_outline]) the species with [constant PlantSpecies.RULE_POOL_DISTANCE] grow round: [method PlantGenerator.make_desert]'s oasis set puts common reed in the shallows and on the shore and rushes behind. Read when the placement is set up, so the pools must be built first.

While [member streaming], tiles within this distance of the centre are placed. Each species is drawn only out to its [member PlantSpecies.visibility_range] (all of the radius when it has none); tiles a tile and a half past the radius are freed. The field publishes the radius as the global shader parameter [code]vegetation_near_radius[/code] (0 when it stops streaming; the last streaming field to publish owns it), so a terrain's far blend can start before the placed plants end.
The [Node3D] streaming follows. Empty: the viewport's camera.

Places tiles around a centre ([member stream_target]) as it moves instead of the whole map at once: each tile is placed on a worker thread, nearest first, together with the larger plants around it that act on it (footprints and crown shade), so it comes out exactly as [method populate] would place it. The maps (canopy, forest floor, far colour) follow the centre and are computed on a worker too. [member populate_on_ready] is ignored while streaming; a new bake of the [member data_map] places everything again.
Width in metres of a tile: one point pattern and one [MultiMeshInstance3D] per mesh per tile, so tiles out of view are culled.

If [code]true[/code], each [method populate] that places canopy crowns publishes canopy closure ([method get_shade_at]) and conifer share ([method get_conifer_at]) on half-metre cells over the data map's rect as the [code]forest_floor_map[/code] and [code]forest_floor_rect[/code] global shader parameters, read by [method get_floor_shader_code]. A field without crowns leaves them as they are, so one field can own the trees while others place the plants.

Path to a [WeatherMap3D]. After each [method populate] the placed canopy species are written to its [member WeatherMap3D.canopy_map] over the data map's rect (about 1 m cells): crown top height in red, leaf area index over 4 in green, taking [member PlantSpecies.canopy_opacity] as [code]1 - exp(-0.5 LAI)[/code]. [method WeatherMap3D.get_canopy_closure_at] then matches [method get_shade_at], and snow, wind and light under the trees all see the same forest. This replaces any canopy map already set there.

Worn paths, each a [Dictionary] with [code]points[/code] ([PackedVector3Array], the path's centre line), [code]width[/code] (metres, default 1.0) and [code]passes[/code] (walkers a year, default 1000). Trampling falls off across a path as a Gaussian with sigma a quarter of its width, over a wider tail (15% of the walkers, three times the sigma), so plants shorten over a metre or so towards the tread. Plants with a [member PlantSpecies.trample_resistance] thin out and grow shorter where passes outweigh it, following Cole's trampling experiments; trees, logs and stone-top plants are never trampled. Changing it repopulates. The world's game trails ([code]WorldStand.get_trails()[/code], published from [method VegetationField3D.make_game_trails]) are worn the same way, on top of these, and followed when they change.
The channel of [member biome_map] that holds this field's biome; -1 ignores the map.
A painted map shared by several fields, one biome a channel. A field's plants are kept by its channel's share, so overlapping paint splits the ground; outside the map the field grows everywhere.
The ground [member biome_map] covers, in metres (x, z, width, depth).
Clears the placed plants.
Places plants round the editor's 3D view in the scene being edited, as in the game, without the game-time systems. Nothing it places is saved.
Places the plants again.

signal.name: populated
signal.description: Emitted after each [method populate], and while [member streaming] each time [method is_stream_idle] becomes [code]true[/code].
